newsitem.title: JAPAN: Former top bureaucrat held in Japan bribe case - NHK.
newsitem.headline: Former top bureaucrat held in Japan bribe case - NHK.

text.p: A former top Japanese bureaucrat was arrested on bribery charges on Wednesday amid allegations that he took 60 million yen ($530,000) in cash from a business executive, NHK public television reported.

Nobuharu Okamitsu, former vice minister at the Health Ministry, is suspected of accepting bribes from a nursing home operator in exchange for influencing decisions on state subsidies to build nursing homes, NHK said.

Besides the cash, Okamitsu is also suspected of receiving a golf club membership worth 9.5 million yen ($84,000), and the loan of two luxury sedans worth seven million yen ($61,900) from Hiroshi Koyama, head of the Aya Fukushi Group, media reports said.

Koyama, arrested on November 18 on suspicion of bribing a subordinate of Okamitsu's at the ministry, has also said he paid some 30 million yen ($265,000) to refurbish Okamitsu's Tokyo apartment, according to media reports.

Okamitsu, 57, is suspected of helping Koyama's welfare firm obtain state subsidies to build specialised institutions for the elderly under a government policy designed to cope with Japan's rapidly greying population. Okamitsu, who resigned as the ministry's top career bureaucrat on November 19, has denied the allegations.

The Health Ministry affair has embarrassed Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's new government. Hashimoto said last week he felt ashamed over a series of scandals which have hurt public confidence in the government. ($1=113 yen)
